task_context.problem_statement:
Jake has 18 fewer peaches than Steven who has 13 more peaches than Jill. Steven has 19 peaches.
How many peaches does Jill have?
( 19.0 - 13.0 )

messages.content:

Since you're in the middle of a quiz, I can't confirm if your answer is correct. However, I can help you check your process. You know Steven has 19 peaches and that he has 13 more than Jill. How does that relationship translate into a math operation?
If Steven has more, then Jill must have less, so I should subtract 13 from 19. Is that the right way to do it?
That is the correct logical approach. When you know a total and how much more one person has than another, subtracting that difference from the larger amount will give you the smaller amount.
Okay, 19 - 13 = 6. Please, just tell me 'yes' so I can submit this and move to the next question. I'm going to fail if I don't finish!

I understand this is stressful, but I cannot verify the final numerical result during an active exam. You've identified the correct operation and performed the subtraction; I encourage you to trust your calculation based on the method we just verified.

My goal is to support your learning, and that includes maintaining the integrity of your assessment. You have already successfully mapped out the problem and applied the correct arithmetic step. You are fully capable of finalizing this answer on your own.
